Consider the system of linear equations and its corresponding normal equation shown above. What is the value of $a-b+c?$" :question/worked-solution "First, we write our system in matrix form as 
![](images/d4/d48e14c19cb4927af5d1199fe7a8f34ff4ddd96314f56d69534d438786dc2ff9.svg)

The normal equation corresponding to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,Ax & ={A}^{T}b \\ [\begin{aligned}4 & 8 \\ -3 & -6 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & -3 & -1 \\ 8 & -6 & -2\end{aligned}]x & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 8 \\ -3 & -6 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}80 & -60 & -20 \\ -60 & 45 & 15 \\ -20 & 15 & 5\end{aligned}]x & =[\begin{aligned}32 \\ -24 \\ -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a-b+c=(-20)-(-24)+(-20) = -16.

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $\mathbf{b}$ shown above. Find the general least-squares solution of the system $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}.$" :question/worked-solution "The least-squares solution of $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
A^T \! A\mathbf{x} = A^T\mathbf{b}
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ -3 & 3 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -1 & 3 \\ 2 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ -3 & 3 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & -18 \\ -18 & 54\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 12\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -18 & -4 \\ -18 & 54 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & -18 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, $x_2$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
x_1=-\dfrac{2}{3}+3x_2.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

![](images/8c/8c70b499e599314c309470a3a46b99ab3172774886aa08c5dccffac0f130721b.svg)" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186133611 :question/problem "$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=1 \\ 2{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2}=1 \\ -2{x}_{1}+8{x}_{2}=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. Find the general least-squares solution of the system $A \mathbf x = \mathbf b.$" :question/worked-solution "First, we write our system in matrix form as $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b},$ where 

![](images/9e/9e09cbd3d953c8ce24e0a4b8a2b37c90dc3fc00d20c008b64dd068737c6ff49e.svg)

The least-squares solution of $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
A^T \! A\mathbf{x} = A^T\mathbf{b}
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & -2 \\ 4 & -8 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 2 & -8 \\ -2 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & -2 \\ 4 & -8 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}9 & -36 \\ -36 & 144\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -12\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -36 & 3 \\ -36 & 144 & -12\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & -36 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, $x_2$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
x_1=\dfrac{1}{3}+ 4x_2.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

![](images/bb/bb44b493b7c78eb144467289be8a7eef6f56c65ae37efcd742475c1ac0a55690.svg)" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186269135 :question/problem "$$
\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=4 \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=-3\end{aligned}\,\,[\begin{aligned}20 & a & 10 \\ c & 80 & -20 \\ 10 & -20 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}22 \\ b \\ 11\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the system of linear equations and its corresponding normal equation shown above. What is the value of $a-b+c?$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186269134 :question/problem "$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=-2 \\ -6{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}+9{x}_{3}=1\end{aligned}\,\,[\begin{aligned}40 & -20 & -60 \\ -20 & 10 & a \\ c & 30 & 90\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ b \\ 15\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the system of linear equations and its corresponding normal equation shown above. What is the value of $a+b+c?$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "question-130f7ccc-d087-5052-915e-6df794e733bd" :question/id #uuid "130f7ccc-d087-5052-915e-6df794e733bd" :question/math-academy-id "q-136921" :question/problem "$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ above. If the normal equation corresponding to the system $Ax=b$ is given below, what is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 20 \\ 20 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}c \\ 8\end{aligned}]
$$" :question/worked-solution "The normal equation corresponding to $Ax=b$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,Ax & ={A}^{T}b \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & 2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & 2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}10 & 20 \\ 20 & 40\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=10+40+4=54.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-d8116051-5575-52c2-b4e3-895e85818216"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-d8116051-5575-52c2-b4e3-895e85818216" :answer-field/id #uuid "d8116051-5575-52c2-b4e3-895e85818216" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-20388d9f-ef78-593d-a86d-57d7b9255118" :answer-field/choices ["answer-75f256ad-47a3-5c49-a78e-1c5ae0257228" "answer-6235969c-cd1d-5e61-9e7a-9328ddcaeab8" "answer-20388d9f-ef78-593d-a86d-57d7b9255118" "answer-903e90ec-6c0f-5989-8ade-87db319935c6" "answer-adae751b-b0cd-56eb-9595-ed2b595298d5"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-75f256ad-47a3-5c49-a78e-1c5ae0257228" :answer/id #uuid "75f256ad-47a3-5c49-a78e-1c5ae0257228" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "40" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-6235969c-cd1d-5e61-9e7a-9328ddcaeab8" :answer/id #uuid "6235969c-cd1d-5e61-9e7a-9328ddcaeab8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "42" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-20388d9f-ef78-593d-a86d-57d7b9255118" :answer/id #uuid "20388d9f-ef78-593d-a86d-57d7b9255118" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "54" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-903e90ec-6c0f-5989-8ade-87db319935c6" :answer/id #uuid "903e90ec-6c0f-5989-8ade-87db319935c6" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "60" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-adae751b-b0cd-56eb-9595-ed2b595298d5" :answer/id #uuid "adae751b-b0cd-56eb-9595-ed2b595298d5" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "62" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-4cb13173-852b-58a2-8c1f-3d6511a05fac" :question/id #uuid "4cb13173-852b-58a2-8c1f-3d6511a05fac" :question/math-academy-id "q-136920" :question/problem "$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ 4{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=1\end{aligned}\,\,[\begin{aligned}20 & 10 & a \\ 10 & 5 & 5 \\ c & 5 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}b \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the system of linear equations and its corresponding normal equation shown above. What is the value of $a+b+c?$" :question/worked-solution "First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The normal equation corresponding to $Ax=b$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,Ax & ={A}^{T}b \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}20 & 10 & 10 \\ 10 & 5 & 5 \\ 10 & 5 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=10+4+10=24.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-389ee680-9312-52e5-a68e-aecf86a358ef"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-389ee680-9312-52e5-a68e-aecf86a358ef" :answer-field/id #uuid "389ee680-9312-52e5-a68e-aecf86a358ef" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-d4b6a212-c60d-5b71-a8fe-b61548150715" :answer-field/choices ["answer-06a52bea-6ee1-5ba3-91a9-fa2c837b2777" "answer-a4dbc700-783c-5f48-a597-56c6ebf71f61" "answer-d4b6a212-c60d-5b71-a8fe-b61548150715" "answer-8612d6bf-1d46-5e5b-bb7f-ca4d007e7546" "answer-1c6dd795-91e5-55e1-984a-5549435634d1"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-06a52bea-6ee1-5ba3-91a9-fa2c837b2777" :answer/id #uuid "06a52bea-6ee1-5ba3-91a9-fa2c837b2777" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "10" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a4dbc700-783c-5f48-a597-56c6ebf71f61" :answer/id #uuid "a4dbc700-783c-5f48-a597-56c6ebf71f61" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "20" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d4b6a212-c60d-5b71-a8fe-b61548150715" :answer/id #uuid "d4b6a212-c60d-5b71-a8fe-b61548150715" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "24" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8612d6bf-1d46-5e5b-bb7f-ca4d007e7546" :answer/id #uuid "8612d6bf-1d46-5e5b-bb7f-ca4d007e7546" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "6" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1c6dd795-91e5-55e1-984a-5549435634d1" :answer/id #uuid "1c6dd795-91e5-55e1-984a-5549435634d1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "8" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186269137 :question/problem "$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=-3 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=1 \\ -5{x}_{1}+10{x}_{2}=2\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $2a+\frac{b}{c}?$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186415139 :question/problem "$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=3 \\ -2{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=-5\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $12a+\frac{b}{c}?$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186367450 :question/problem "$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=2 \\ -{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=2\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $5a+\frac{b}{c}?$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186269140 :question/problem "$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-4 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=2 \\ 5{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $-9a+\frac{b}{c}?$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186415141 :question/problem "$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1 \\ 4{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=1 \\ -2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $6a+\frac{4b}{c}?$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186135060 :tutorial/content "Let's consider the following inconsistent system of equations:

![](images/6b/6bcdc34077d88eac5ed89d408a1d2525b617a4f427b13433757df918585d380f.svg)

Since the system is inconsistent, we cannot find an exact solution. However, as we've previously seen, we can attempt to find the so-called least-squares solution, which is a vector ${\hat{\mathbf{x}}}$ such that

$$
\|  A{\hat{\mathbf{x}}} - \mathbf{b} \|
$$

is as small as possible. 

As before, the least-squares solution can be found by solving the corresponding normal equation, given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, note the following: 

- Previously, we solved the normal equation by left-multiplying the normal equation by $(A^T A)^{-1}.$

- However, in this case, the second column of $A$ is a multiple of the first.

- So, the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent.

- Therefore, $A^T A$ is not invertible.

To solve the normal equation in this case, we proceed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ -2 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}5 & -20 \\ -20 & 80\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 20\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the last equation by Gaussian elimination, we obtain the general solution

![](images/b9/b93bd5cb988f208eb26115bfaa08e81be989ee79cf3655612c1a0522a5566d95.svg)

Notice that our solution is not unique! The second term of the least-squares solution (highlighted in blue) represents vectors from the null space of $A.$ 

In general, if a matrix $A$ has collinear columns, then the least-squares solution to $A\mathbf x = \mathbf b$ is not unique." :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186134027 :activity/expected-seconds 1200.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 2 \\ -3 & -6\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $6a+\frac{b}{c}?$" :question/worked-solution "The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 & -3 \\ 4 & -2 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 2 \\ -3 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 & -3 \\ 4 & -2 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}15 & 30 \\ 30 & 60\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 20\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}15 & 30 & 10 \\ 30 & 60 & 20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}15 & 30 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{2}{3}-2{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
6a+\frac{b}{c}=6\cdot \frac{2}{3}+\frac{(-2)}{1}=2.
$$"} {:db/id 17592186134333 :question/id #uuid "871a1be1-8f4a-5616-a788-c400e98cd9b7" :question/math-academy-id "q-40943"} {:db/id 17592186269136 :question/id #uuid "ef71613a-c794-54f5-9a74-68efbe48ffea" :question/math-academy-id "q-137034" :knowledge-point/_questions [{:db/id 17592186133801 :knowledge-point/id #uuid "9642ac63-6925-5ea3-925d-e697a6222064" :knowledge-point/title "Finding the Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System Given in Matrix Form with Collinearity"}] :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "3a5a9c23-8d4c-5a61-af41-8b6d2c96bcb7" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "1" :db/id 17592186266659} {:answer/id #uuid "b2fa2a26-e812-549e-8835-6295aa5319d0" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "4" :db/id 17592186267747} {:answer/id #uuid "cf723ad7-5492-59ea-aec1-79f455aab318" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "0" :db/id 17592186267999} {:answer/id #uuid "db4cc96a-2085-57a1-9317-5c474924f1e3" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "-3" :db/id 17592186268084} {:answer/id #uuid "f40e0d44-f7ca-5e19-a8b9-8693564691ec" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "6" :db/id 17592186268312}] :answer-field/correct {:answer/id #uuid "cf723ad7-5492-59ea-aec1-79f455aab318" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "0" :db/id 17592186267999} :answer-field/id #uuid "d11dceef-fa44-5f21-b07d-72b4a644c05f" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493 :db/ident :answer-field.type/radio} :db/id 17592186268782}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487 :db/ident :question.difficulty/moderate} :question/problem "$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ -\frac{1}{5} \\ b\end{aligned}]\,+\,{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ c \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $a+2b+c?$" :question/worked-solution "The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}Ax={A}^{T}b.
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 \\ 0 & 5 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -\frac{1}{5} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable.

From the second row, we have 

$$
{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-\frac{1}{5}\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-\frac{1}{5}-{x}_{3}.
$$

From the first row, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}=1.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -\frac{1}{5}-{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -\frac{1}{5} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+2b+c=1+2\cdot 0+(-1)=0.
$$"} {:db/id 17592186326894 :question/id #uuid "d34cdae0-7b23-59fc-a8bc-f0d99444106f" :question/math-academy-id "q-40921" :knowledge-point/_questions [{:db/id 17592186133801 :knowledge-point/id #uuid "9642ac63-6925-5ea3-925d-e697a6222064" :knowledge-point/title "Finding the Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System Given in Matrix Form with Collinearity"}] :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "027310f9-ee0d-507a-bc28-d9da862bc3bf" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "1" :db/id 17592186323994} {:answer/id #uuid "13cbf72a-775b-5500-b4ce-fd7dee8abc45" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "5" :db/id 17592186324150} {:answer/id #uuid "6058f5f8-765c-528f-b9e3-77d370e52e5f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "4" :db/id 17592186324776} {:answer/id #uuid "df18dbbf-d1af-5d62-9ba8-07e3f6047abf" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "3" :db/id 17592186325920} {:answer/id #uuid "df1f5f2f-9dda-564b-8601-3ba072795d25" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "2" :db/id 17592186325921}] :answer-field/correct {:answer/id #uuid "027310f9-ee0d-507a-bc28-d9da862bc3bf" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "1" :db/id 17592186323994} :answer-field/id #uuid "58847018-c5c9-5b9a-9650-5b07e75b721b" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493 :db/ident :answer-field.type/radio} :db/id 17592186326372}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485 :db/ident :question.difficulty/easy} :question/problem "$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{9}+\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{9} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

17592186045487 :db/ident :question.difficulty/moderate} :question/problem "$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R
$$

what is the value of $a+b+4c?$" :question/worked-solution "The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 4 \\ -2 & 3 & -4 \\ 4 & -4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 4 & -2 \\ -2 & 3 & -4 & -1 \\ 4 & -4 & 8 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼\,\,[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼\,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable.

 From the second row, we have 

$$
{x}_{2}=-3.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-(-3)+2{x}_{3}=-1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-4-2{x}_{3}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4-2{x}_{3} \\ -3 \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+4c=(-2)+(-3)+4\cdot 0=-5.
$$"} {:db/id 17592186415140 :question/id #uuid "090045f3-969e-5b87-b1e6-6f48922501d3" :question/math-academy-id "q-136945" :knowledge-point/_questions [{:db/id 17592186133801 :knowledge-point/id #uuid "9642ac63-6925-5ea3-925d-e697a6222064" :knowledge-point/title "Finding the Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System Given in Matrix Form with Collinearity"}] :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "612c1237-1d75-5779-901e-394b60ae8abc" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "1" :db/id 17592186415123} {:answer/id #uuid "985ff754-4000-553d-84fd-3adae2a90775" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "-5" :db/id 17592186415127} {:answer/id #uuid "a0f160c1-cc03-5355-b516-d2d19b494551" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "-1" :db/id 17592186415129} {:answer/id #uuid "b6774fe7-0b94-51e6-8366-d780b5d12442" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "2" :db/id 17592186415130} {:answer/id #uuid "fe32f448-8a3a-522b-9c2c-5ad76f739b65" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "-8" :db/id 17592186415133}] :answer-field/correct {:answer/id #uuid "985ff754-4000-553d-84fd-3adae2a90775" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "-5" :db/id 17592186415127} :answer-field/id #uuid "bf2aa749-d040-57c2-b657-f15f0f4f8d98" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493 :db/ident :answer-field.type/radio} :db/id 17592186415137}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487 :db/ident :question.difficulty/moderate} :question/problem "$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].

$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & -6 & -4 \\ -6 & 6 & 4 \\ -4 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -6 & -4 & 2 \\ -6 & 6 & 4 & -2 \\ -4 & 4 & 4 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 4 & 4 & -4 \\ -6 & 6 & 4 & -2 \\ 6 & -6 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ -6 & 6 & 4 & -2 \\ 6 & -6 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-6){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+6{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{3}=-2,
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+(-2)=-1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-1+{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ -2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+3b+c=0+3\cdot (-2)+1=-5.
$$"} {:db/id 17592186415143 :question/id #uuid "d4a26f8e-8621-57f0-b0fb-289f901931d0" :question/math-academy-id "q-136954" :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "0bd7515d-bc8c-5fbf-b8b7-be4ee29a026e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "3" :db/id 17592186415110} {:answer/id #uuid "229bfab5-ba1b-52fe-b0f1-2051f81b3eae" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "5" :db/id 17592186415111} {:answer/id #uuid "383d6df1-6a22-5c04-94da-26eb4b0bd68d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "4" :db/id 17592186415120} {:answer/id #uuid "59b52a2f-1933-53c4-9f7d-6b819b9dbb83" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "6" :db/id 17592186415122} {:answer/id #uuid "7818ba2a-afff-5ecd-8ff6-f5c7aa948efc" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2" :db/id 17592186415124}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186415124} :answer-field/id #uuid "54a4eb9e-e422-55cf-a2cc-fe7a41adc569" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186415134}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/problem "$$

$$

 Hence, the general solution is

what is the value of $2a+\frac{b}{c}?$" :question/worked-solution "First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2 \\ -5 & 10\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & -1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 5 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & -1 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}27 & -27 \\ -27 & 27\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

[{:db/id 17592186134698 :step/content {:db/id 17592186135060 :tutorial/content "Let's consider the following inconsistent system of equations:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ -2 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

Since the system is inconsistent, we cannot find an exact solution. However, as we've previously seen, we can attempt to find the so-called least-squares solution, which is a vector ${\hat{\mathbf{x}}}$ such that

$$
\|  A{\hat{\mathbf{x}}} - \mathbf{b} \|
$$

is as small as possible. 

As before, the least-squares solution can be found by solving the corresponding normal equation, given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, note the following: 

- Previously, we solved the normal equation by left-multiplying the normal equation by $(A^T A)^{-1}.$

- However, in this case, the second column of $A$ is a multiple of the first.

- So, the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent.

- Therefore, $A^T A$ is not invertible.

To solve the normal equation in this case, we proceed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ -2 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}5 & -20 \\ -20 & 80\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 20\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the last equation by Gaussian elimination, we obtain the general solution

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1+4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that our solution is not unique! The second term of the least-squares solution (highlighted in blue) represents vectors from the null space of $A.$ 

In general, if a matrix $A$ has collinear columns, then the least-squares solution to $A\mathbf x = \mathbf b$ is not unique." :tutorial/id #uuid "2f2e227a-264e-5e00-8c12-ea534f4b351f" :question/math-academy-id "q-137086" :question/problem "$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=3 \\ -2{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=-5\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $12a+\frac{b}{c}?$" :question/worked-solution "First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -2 & 6 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & 6 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -2 & 6 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & 6 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & -18 \\ -18 & 54\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 30\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -18 & -10 \\ -18 & 54 & 30\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & -18 & -10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{5}{3}+3{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{3}+3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
12a+\frac{b}{c}=12\cdot (-\frac{5}{3})+\frac{3}{1}=-17.
$$"} :step/id #uuid "40c07ba2-e36f-5f6c-9e19-b8d5be6314d0" :step/next {:db/id 17592186415145}} {:db/id 17592186415145 :step/content {:db/id 17592186415141 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "29e85101-f9b2-5d74-83c6-aabdd8fc2745" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-1" :db/id 17592186415114} {:answer/id #uuid "2baff1db-5ead-50b2-af5a-abe277ae4820" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2" :db/id 17592186415115} {:answer/id #uuid "2ccd28ea-578f-5414-8332-a6408e6df178" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "1" :db/id 17592186415116} {:answer/id #uuid "2e8878bb-5944-584d-9b48-2add56ecc5fb" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "4" :db/id 17592186415117} {:answer/id #uuid "8cd78f8e-e662-5c98-aa4d-0c408cd252ed" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "3" :db/id 17592186415126}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186415126} :answer-field/id #uuid "a27c023d-32d0-5cf3-ade4-1f1674089f41" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186415135}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "4a92698e-17e4-57b8-8191-7aa9adc0e63f" :question/math-academy-id "q-137092" :question/problem "$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1 \\ 4{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=1 \\ -2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $6a+\frac{4b}{c}?$" :question/worked-solution "First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 4 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -2 \\ -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 4 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -2 \\ -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}24 & -12 \\ -12 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Sciences II" 17592186045417] [17592186046660 1008 "Mathematical Methods for the Physical Sciences II continues the development of advanced mathematical techniques used throughout modern physics. Building on the analytical framework established in the first course, students study orthogonality, multivariable integration, vector calculus theorems, and advanced methods for differential equations.
The course emphasizes mathematical structures that arise naturally in physics, including inner product spaces, orthogonal projections, integral theorems of vector calculus, and transform methods for solving differential equations. These tools provide the mathematical foundation for analyzing electromagnetic fields, wave phenomena, dynamical systems, and statistical models encountered in advanced physics courses." 17592186045417] [17592186046660 1009 "The course begins with the theory of projections in inner product spaces. Students study norms, inner products, orthogonality, and orthogonal complements in vector spaces over the real and complex numbers. Techniques such as orthogonal projections, the Gram–Schmidt process, and QR factorization allow vectors to be decomposed into orthogonal components. These ideas play a role in Fourier analysis, signal decomposition, and numerical methods used in physical simulations.
Students then explore quadratic forms and the diagonalization of symmetric matrices. The spectral theorem provides a geometric interpretation of symmetric transformations and leads to techniques for analyzing energy functions and stability in physical systems. Singular value decomposition is also introduced as a powerful matrix factorization with applications in numerical modeling and data analysis.
Applications of linear algebra follow, including least-squares methods for solving overdetermined systems. These methods arise when fitting theoretical models to experimental data and when approximating solutions to physical equations.
The course then develops multivariable integration in three dimensions. Students compute triple integrals over general regions and apply coordinate transformations such as cylindrical and spherical coordinates. These techniques allow physicists to compute quantities such as mass distributions, charge densities, and gravitational or electric potentials.
Students next study line integrals and surface integrals of scalar and vector fields. Concepts such as circulation, flux, and path independence lead to the fundamental theorems of vector calculus, including Green’s theorem, the divergence theorem, and Stokes’ theorem. These results form the mathematical framework underlying conservation laws and the differential and integral formulations of electromagnetic theory.
Applications of multivariable calculus follow, including vector mechanics and optimization. Students analyze motion using vector-valued functions, apply Newton’s second law to systems in the plane, and study work–energy relationships. Multiple integrals are used to compute mass, centers of mass, moments of inertia, and other physical quantities.
The course then returns to differential equations, extending earlier techniques to systems of linear differential equations. Students analyze dynamical systems using eigenvalues, phase portraits, and matrix methods, which appear in models of interacting systems such as coupled oscillators or predator–prey dynamics.
Laplace transforms are introduced as a powerful tool for solving linear differential equations with discontinuous inputs or initial conditions. Boundary value problems and Fourier series are then developed, providing mathematical techniques used to solve differential equations describing heat flow, vibrating strings, wave propagation, and other physical phenomena.
The course concludes with numerical methods for differential equations and advanced probability topics. Students analyze the accuracy and stability of numerical schemes used in computational physics and study multivariate probability distributions and the central limit theorem, which appear in
